a.i

Red giant has a much larger radius/luminosity than the Sun;
Red giant has a cooler surface temperature than the Sun.

Award [1] for each distinct, correct property difference.

a.ii

The Sun is a main sequence star, while a red giant is a post-main sequence star.

b.i

Energy released = BE(products) - BE(reactants) = 12×7.680 - (8×7.062 + 4×7.074) = 92.160 - (56.496 + 28.296) = 7.368 MeV. Award [1] for correct method (difference in total binding energies). Award [1] for correct answer. Accept 7.37 MeV.

Answer must be in MeV.

b.ii

Curve in first quadrant starting at a high positive value for small r; Correct 1/r shape, always positive and approaching the r-axis asymptotically.

Award [1] for starting high and being in the first quadrant. Award [1] for correct decreasing shape asymptotic to the r-axis.

b.iii

The negative of the electric field strength / -E.

Accept 'negative of the electric field'. 'Electric field' alone is incorrect.

b.iv

= = k()(Q_α)/r = (8.99×10⁹ × 8 × (1.60×10⁻¹⁹)²) / 4.5×10⁻¹⁵ = 4.09×10⁻¹³ J;
This is 4.09×10⁻¹³ J / (1.60×10⁻¹³ J/MeV) ≈ 2.56 MeV.
Award [1] for setting KE=PE with correct charges. Award [1] for correct calculation and conversion to MeV. Accept 2.6 MeV.

c.i

Extremely high temperature AND extremely high density/pressure.

Both conditions are required.

c.ii

The decay constant implies a very short half-life (T½ ≈ 8.7×10⁻¹⁷ s), so the Be-8 nucleus is extremely unstable;
A high density of alpha particles and high collision rate is needed for fusion to occur before the Be-8 nucleus decays.

Award [1] for linking decay constant to instability/short lifetime. Award [1] for linking this to the need for a high collision rate.

d.ii

Shows / = ( / ) = 625, so = 625 . OR / = ( ω_f²) / ( ω_i²) = (1/625) × 625² = 625, so = 625 .

Award [1] for correct method/reasoning. Award [1] for final answer.

d.iii

Any two of:
- Gravitational potential energy decreases.
- Rotational kinetic energy increases.
- Internal/thermal energy increases.
- Energy is radiated away (as neutrinos/photons).

Award [1] for each correct energy change identified.
